text:
julie_support: Heads up — incoming escalation. Customer sees intermittent 502s hitting /v1/generate. They gave an approximate time 2026-03-16T14:21:33Z and request_id=9f1e2c4a7b1d4f23. They also pasted a curl they ran and want server-side logs + reproduction help. Can ops grab logs? :eyes:

alex_r: Can you paste the exact request_id (full UUID if available) and the region? Also would be great to get the raw curl they used so we can reproduce.

julie_support: Full request_id they sent: 9f1e2c4a-7b1d-4f23-9a2b-0c5d6e7f8a9b. Region: us-east-1. Customer curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"summarize this...","max_tokens":256}'
```
They say it fails ~1/20 requests, usually returns 502 after ~1.2s.

sam_b: For ops log search, run something like this in Kibana/Logs: (replace time window +/-5m around reported time)
```
service:api AND request_id:"9f1e2c4a-7b1d-4f23-9a2b-0c5d6e7f8a9b" | sort @timestamp desc
```
Note: our request-level logs are retained for 30 days in prod. If the customer timestamp is older than that we might only have traces/metrics.

alex_r: Ran a quick search on prod index in us-east-1 — found 3 entries within 2 minutes of the timestamp:
```
[2026-03-16T14:21:33.128Z] ERROR api.gateway request_id=9f1e2c4a-... status=502 upstream_t=1187ms err="upstream returned 502"
[2026-03-16T14:21:34.390Z] WARN  inference.worker request_id=9f1e2c4a-... kv_cache_miss model=redwood-large seq=256
[2026-03-16T14:21:34.500Z] INFO  router.fallback request_id=9f1e2c4a-... routed_to=redwood-large-quantized
```
Looks like upstream (runtime) hit an error after a long upstream tokenization step. I'll pull a debug bundle from the node that served that request.

opsbot: To generate a debug bundle for a specific request run (internal only):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_SERVICE_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal.ops.redwood/debug-bundle?request_id=9f1e2c4a-7b1d-4f23-9a2b-0c5d6e7f8a9b&range=2m" \
  -o debug-9f1e2c4a.tar.gz
```
This will include sanitized logs, runtime metrics, and a minimal repro trace. Keep the bundle internal (PII scrubbed).

maria_k: Also ask the customer to re-run with --dump-headers or `-v` and paste the response headers if possible. We need the x-request-id from their client and any upstream timing headers (x-upstream-time). If they can reproduce, ask for a short curl that triggers the 502 and we can attach to the bundle.

julie_support: Sending the steps to the customer now and asking them to re-run with -v. Will upload the debug bundle here once ops link is ready. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

alex_r: One more note — if we don't find logs (older than 30d) escalate to infra for trace sampling dumps; otherwise we should have full request traces for that ID.
